about: Part of the reference catalogue: designed experiments from chapters 1 and 2 of Schmidt and Launsby,
Understanding Industrial Designed Experiments, for testing that software reproduces them. source: the citation,
with what was read and when. experiments: each worked example with data (factors, responses, runs exactly as
printed, in the printed order), where it is printed, and expected: every number the book prints for it, as
printed text, with where it is printed (a page and a quotation) and check: how to recompute it, or manual, the
reason it is not recomputed. A check with a disagreement records a number known not to reproduce and why. Where
the book prints each run's readings beside their average and standard deviation, the runs keep all three as
printed: each run's average and standard deviation is checked against its readings (a check's summary names
the readings), and the book's tables of averages at each level are worked from the columns the book worked
from, which each entry's notes name. The book prints each effect Δ as the difference of the two averages it has
rounded, so an effect's check carries of_rounded: 2, the rounding of both. design.treatment_factors counts the factors varied as treatments: 0 for
a record, 1 for a one-factor comparison. designs: fractions whose generators and aliases the book states.
not_captured: what in these pages is not an experiment with data. Read with
recomputes every number that has a check.
